Prevention: NARONUTS 1R and 2T Plant at the onset of rains
Remove volunteer groundnuts crops in the field prior to planting
Practice crop rotation i.e. groundnuts with cereals (sorghum, maize and millet).
Use appropriate spacing; for erect/bunchy types (e.g.Serenut 6T, RedBeauty), plant 45 cm between the rows and 7.5 - 10 cm between the plants.
Serenuts 7 to 14 series) plant 45 cm between the rows and : 10 - 15cm between the plants
Monitoring: Scout for the aphid vector weekly starting at 5 days post emergency to 50% flowering.
Look out for stunted plants with chlorotic (yellowish) curled and puckered leaflets with dark green patches for the
Green groundnut rosette, plants are stunted and bushy having dark-green leaflets with mild and narrow chlorotic streaks, reduced size and margins rolled outward
Use yellow stickers to monitor presence of aphid.
Start controlling when 10% of the plant has an average of 10 aphids per plant
Direct Control: Remove rosetted plants from the field during the season and burn or bury at least 15 cm depth
Destroy volunteer groundnut plants and weeds
Restrictions: No chemical control for the disease but for the vector
Protective gear while mixing pesticides and spraying
Protective gear while mixing pesticides and spraying
Dimethoate to control vector population 14 days after emergence (usually 5mls per 2 litres of water, but read the label for instructions) and then at 10-day intervals for a total of four sprays.
